stem:
Table 4.1 gives the enthalpy changes of hydration, $\Delta H_{\text{hyd}}$, of three ions, $\text{F}^-$, $\text{K}^+$ and $\text{Ca}^{2+}$.

Table 4.1

| ion | $\Delta H_{\text{hyd}} / \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ |
| :--- | :--- |
| $\text{F}^-$ | $-506$ |
| $\text{K}^+$ | $-322$ |
| $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ | $-1650$ |

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Explain the relative magnitudes of the enthalpy changes of hydration of $\text{K}^+$ and $\text{Ca}^{2+}$.

parts.label: (a)(iv)
parts.text:
The lattice energy, $\Delta H_{\text{latt}}$, of calcium fluoride, $\text{CaF}_2$, is $-2602\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

Calculate the enthalpy change of solution, $\Delta H_{\text{sol}}$, in $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$, of $\text{CaF}_2$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
The formation of $\text{CaF}_2$ at $298\text{ K}$ is shown.

$$\text{Ca(s)} + \text{F}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow \text{CaF}_2\text{(s)} \quad \Delta H^{\ominus} = -1214\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$
$$\Delta G^{\ominus} = -1162\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$

Calculate the entropy change, $\Delta S^{\ominus}$, in $\text{J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$, for this reaction.
